title: Open Values Challenge Set v0.1
description: Worked examples for showing a reader the best case for a different choice: for a category, a likely weighting and its opposite, the top pick under each, and the sourced facts to show. It is kept by hand at content/challenge/index.json; the challenge audit reranks every example against the current data, and pipeline/build_challenge.js builds an index from it.

format.description: Always "open-values-challenge-set". Tells a reader which Open Values format this is.

version.description: The version of the challenge set format this file follows. Must start with 0.1.0.

standard.description: Always "open-values-standard", the standard this format belongs to.

updated.description: The date the file was last changed, as YYYY-MM-DD.

purpose.description: A sentence or two saying what this file is for.

principles.description: The rules challenge features follow, one short sentence each, such as "challenge is calm and dismissible".

algorithms.description: The methods that pick what to show a reader, each with what it reads, what it produces, and what it must not do.

instances.description: The sites and apps that can show challenges, and how visible each makes them by default.

cases.description: Worked examples: a category ranked under a reader's likely weighting and under the opposite one, with the expected top pick of each. The challenge audit reranks each case and fails if the top picks differ.

contraryTags.description: Sourced facts that a challenge can show: weaknesses of a likely top pick, or strengths of the opposite pick.

note.description: One or two sentences saying what the source shows.

source.description: The web address of the source, starting with http:// or https://.

asof.description: When the source was checked, as a year such as "2026", or a year and month such as "2026-08".

additionalProperties.description: The weight for one criterion, from 0 (ignored) to 5 (counts most).

id.description: A short name for the method, such as "opposite-view" or "steelman".

label.description: The name to show readers, such as "Opposite view".

summary.description: One or two sentences saying what the method does.

inputs.description: The fields the method reads, named by their path in a case, such as "userView.weights".

outputs.description: The fields the method produces, named by their path in a case, such as "oppositeView.expectedTop".

mustNot.description: Things the method must never do, one sentence each, such as "Do not store or infer a user's private values."

id.description: A short name for the site or app, such as "kosplora".

label.description: The name to show readers, such as "Kosplora".

role.description: What part the site plays for challenge features, as a short label such as "flagship-learning-instance".

status.description: How far along the site is, when it is not yet live, such as "format-seed".

challengeDefault.description: How visible the challenge feature is by default on this site: available (there if asked for), prominent (shown alongside results), or primary (the main thing the site shows).

surfaces.description: The places on the site where a challenge can appear, such as "verdict", "category" or "entry".

label.description: A short name for the weighting, such as "Privacy and openness first".

weights.description: How much each criterion counts in this view, keyed by criterion key from the category dataset, such as { "privacy": 5, "safety": 2 }. Each weight runs from 0 (ignored) to 5 (counts most).

expectedTop.description: The code of the entry this weighting ranks first in the category dataset, such as "jan-ai".

sourceTag.description: For the opposite view, the id of the contrary tag that backs its top pick, such as "ai-assistants/chatgpt/accessibility". It must be the highest-scoring opposite-view-strength tag for that entry.

forEntity.description: The code of the entry the weakness is about. It must be the user view's expected top pick.

axis.description: The criterion key the weakness is on, such as "safety". The user view must weight it at 2 or below.

sourceTag.description: The id of the contrary tag that backs the weakness. It must be the lowest-scoring steelman-weakness tag for that entry on an axis the user view weights at 2 or below.

framing.description: The sentence a reader sees about the weakness, at least 40 characters, written fairly and without dismissive words.

id.description: A unique name for this case, in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.

category.description: The id of the category dataset the case ranks, such as "ai-assistants".

label.description: A short title for the case, such as "Open/local AI assistant versus managed safety".

reads.description: The one sentence a reader sees, 24 to 140 characters. The challenge audit requires it to start with "The strongest case the other way: ".

userView.description: The weighting a reader is likely to hold, and which entry it puts on top.

oppositeView.description: The opposite weighting, which entry it puts on top, and the sourced fact that backs that entry.

steelman.description: The strongest sourced weakness of the user view's top pick, on a criterion that view barely weights.

id.description: A unique id for the fact, written as category/entity/axis, such as "ai-assistants/jan-ai/safety".

category.description: The id of the category dataset the fact belongs to.

entity.description: The code of the entry the fact is about, as it appears in the category dataset.

axis.description: The criterion key the fact is about, such as "safety". It must be a criterion of the category.

polarity.description: Whether the fact is a weakness of a likely top pick (steelman-weakness) or a strength of the opposite pick (opposite-view-strength).

score.description: The entry's score on that criterion, from 0 to 100. The challenge audit checks it equals the score in the generated category dataset.

source.description: Where the fact comes from. The challenge audit checks it matches the source recorded for that score in the generated category dataset.
